messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: gpu-node-7 - repeated container restarts + CUDA OOMs detected at 2025-10-12T03:12:25Z. Creating incident thread in #incidents.

maya: seeing a burst of prefetch activity in the runtime logs, but node headroom metric still reports ~6.1GiB. weird fragmentation?

ana: confirmed: telemetry shows allocator headroom = 6.1 GiB but recent alloc failures trying to grab ~2.7 GiB chunks. pattern looks like reserved blocks + fragmentation.

ryan: relevant log snippet:
```
2025-10-12T03:12:24Z ERROR cuda: failed to allocate 2818047232 bytes: out of memory
2025-10-12T03:12:24Z WARN allocator: request=2.62GiB available_chunks=[1.5GiB, 1.2GiB, 512MiB]
2025-10-12T03:12:24Z INFO kv-reserve: sparepool_total=8GiB sparepool_free=1.2GiB
2025-10-12T03:12:24Z INFO headroom_metric=6.1GiB
```

maya: stack points at kv-cache prefetch thread taking transient reserved blocks during warmup. if prefetch grabs many small blocks it can cause fragmentation which prevents large contiguous allocs despite headroom.

ana: quick mitigation plan: 1) disable prefetch on the affected pool, 2) cordon + drain gpu-node-7, 3) restart runtime container to clear transient reserves, 4) monitor alloc_fail_count.

will: oncall handoff -> ana to will at 03:45Z, will take lead. :handshake:

will: executing mitigations now: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-7 && kubectl drain gpu-node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --force`

ops-bot: drain initiated for node gpu-node-7. pods evicted: 12. pods pending reschedule: 3.

will: applied temporary config: `REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=off` on runtime pool via rollout patch, restarting runtime pods: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime`

maya: prefetch disabled on the pool, confirming via metrics: prefetch_active_threads -> 0 across pool.

ryan: restarted runtime container on replacement node. quick sanity check logs show no immediate OOMs and allocator headroom now reports 5.8GiB matched to free mem.

ana: customer impact summary: ~12k requests failed (mostly short-lived 503s) over a 7m window during the node flap; impacted customers: corp-analytics (batch reruns), prod-chat (tail latency spikes). CS alerted and initial messages sent.

will: putting incident into monitoring mode for 30m. if no regressions, we'll mark mitigated and start postmortem. tagging infra for deeper allocator/fracture analysis: @infra-team 

maya: adding a temporary alert: alloc_fail_count > 5/min -> paging oncall and auto-disable-prefetch policy. also adding a short-term histogram to capture largest_free_block size.

ryan: note for postmortem: possible root causes to investigate: KV cache double-reserve during warmup, small-block churn in sparepool, CUDA driver-level allocation granularity. gather coredumps and `nvidia-smi -q` snapshots from gpu-node-7 before recycle.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. responders: will, maya, ana, ryan. Please update the incident doc with timeline, commands run, and customer notifications. :white_check_mark:
